text.p: Rare Hospitality International Inc shares were cut by Interstate/Johnson Lane to neutral from buy on Tuesday.
-- Late Monday, the company said it expects second quarter earnings to be lower than analysts' estimates, partly as a result of increased restaurant-level costs of food and labor.
-- Shares were down to 11-3/8 from 16-1/6 in pre-opening trading from Monday's Nasdaq close.

-- Rare Hospitality, which runs Longhorn Steakhouses and Bugaboo Creek, said it expects second quarter earnings of $0.16 - $0.18, about 35 percent below the $0.25 - $0.27 consensus analysts' estimate.
-- Analyst Stephanie Haggerty cut her 1997 profit estimate to $0.94 from $1.15 and 1998 to $1.21 from $1.45.

-- In a report, she said Rare cited three major problems at its Longhorn Steakhouses: higher food costs, higher labor costs, and costs associated with a facility and food persentation upgrade program.
-- Although the company said it has made changes to correct the situation, "we do not believe a quick earnings rebound is likely in the current industry environment," Haggerty said in a release.
-- Shares were off 5-1/16 to 11 in early trading.
